learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving problems typical of engineering.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and the technologies and tools of Industrial Engineering into their professional activities.
Know and apply the knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and use of the principles of Mechanics in Mechanical Engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: General concepts and parts of mechanics
Moment of a couple of forces
Equilibrium of a rigid body in two dimensions
Equilibrium of a rigid body in three dimensions
Types of constraints: fixed supports, articulated joints, and fixed ends
Types of systems: Isostatic, Hyperstatic, partially constrained, and improperly constrained
Centers of gravity of a two-dimensional body
Calculation of centers of gravity by integration
Centers of gravity of three-dimensional bodies
Calculation of centers of gravity of volumes by integration
Second order moments. Radius of gyration
Central ellipse of inertia. Principal axes and principal moments
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum weighted score of 5 out of 10 is required. Additionally, a minimum of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in the June ordinary exam. Continuous assessment scores are valid only for the ordinary call, while laboratory scores apply to both ordinary and extraordinary calls and are carried over to subsequent years. If a student achieves the maximum score in the global exam (either ordinary or extraordinary), their final course grade will be 10. For the extraordinary call, the final grade consists of 10% from the Laboratory and 90% from the July Extraordinary Exam, with a minimum of 4 points required in the July exam.
